pageIntroduction: Use this tool to create an accessibility planning path for your meeting or event.
This tool is for organizers, hosts, moderators, presenters, facilitators, and technical support staff.
See the Best practices for accessible meetings and events (opens in a new tab) guide for examples, timelines, budget considerations, and platform or venue guidance that go beyond this checklist tool.

questionnaireInstructions: Answer the three questions, then select Show my planning path. Questions 1 and 2 require an answer; additional session features in question 2 and quesion 3 are optional. You can edit your answers and rebuild the checklist at any time.

notes: Use for meetings and events where all participants attend in the same physical location.

sections.title: 1.2  Virtual only meeting or event checklist

sections.title: 2.1  Audience of 1–25 — checklist
notes: Use for 1–25 participants. Add session-feature and additional-consideration checklists as applicable; small does not mean low risk.

sections.title: 2.2  Training, workshops, and presentations - checklist
notes: Use for: training sessions, workshops, briefings, demonstrations, and other sessions where content, slides, or participant learning are central.

sections.title: 2.3  Larger meeting (26 to 100 participants) - checklist
notes: Use for 26–100 participants. Add the high-risk or testing checklist and any selected session features and considerations.

sections.title: 2.4  Town hall, organization-wide session, or audience of 101 or more — checklist
notes: Use for 101 or more participants, or a town hall or organization-wide session at any size. Add selected session features and considerations.

sections.title: 2.5  Public, formal, or high-risk events checklist
notes: Use for: public events, high-profile events, formal sessions, technical briefings, legal or policy-heavy events, bilingual events, interpreted events, and recorded events.

sections.title: 3.1  Core accessibility checklist
notes: Included in every planning path.

sections.title: 3.2  Accessibility contact and follow-up checklist
notes: Included in every planning path.

sections.title: 3.3  Bilingual and official languages checklist
notes: Use when the meeting or event is bilingual, interpreted, or involves both official languages.

sections.title: 3.4  Large meetings, public, or high-risk events checklist
notes: Added for 26 or more participants, town halls or organization-wide sessions, public/formal sessions, explicit high-risk content, or recording the session. Sharing notes alone does not trigger this checklist.

sections.title: 3.5  Visual content checklist
notes: Added when visual content is selected. Pre-recorded media has its own checklist with instructions for audio-only and video content.

Note: the delivery format and event type checklists above may also include context-specific reminders to describe visuals (for example, printed materials in a room, or content shared on screen). This item is a general reminder shown whenever visual content applies, and is not meant to replace those more specific items.

sections.title: 3.6  Recording and follow-up materials checklist
notes: Added for recording or shared follow-up materials. Recording-specific actions apply only when recording is selected; official-record actions also require the Public/formal session feature.

sections.title: 3.7  Indigenous, cultural, and community considerations checklist
notes: Added automatically when your planning path includes Indigenous, cultural, or community considerations.

sections.title: 3.8  Accessibility supports checklist
notes: Added when accessibility supports are selected. Apply only the instructions for services you will use; online platform and lobby checks apply to virtual or hybrid delivery.

sections.title: 3.9  Presenter coordination checklist
notes: Added when Multiple presenters is selected.

sections.title: 3.10  Accessible interaction checklist
notes: Added when Interaction is selected.

notes: Added when Pre-recorded content is selected; use the actions appropriate to audio-only, silent video, or video with audio.
